First task: examine the data for cleanliness issues

  • Realizing that a lot of the variables in the dataset are missing like 50% of the rows…so let’s first rank all the possible Y variables (in ‘ecosystem vitality on page 3’) and X variables (in ‘climate change on page 4’) based on how many NA rows there are, then choose based on a tradeoff between relevance and # of missing rows.
  • I’m using 2019, which is the last year with fisheries data (see page 130/131)
ecosystem_vars <- c(
  # Biodiversity & Habitat
  "MKP", "MHP", "MPE", "PAR", "SPI", "TBN", "TKP", "PAE", "PHL", "RLI", "SHI", "BER",
  
  # Forests
  "PFL", "IFL", "FCL", "TCG", "FLI",
  
  # Fisheries
  "FSS", "FCD", "BTZ", "BTO", "RMS",
  
  # Air Pollution
  "OEB", "OEC", "NXA", "SDA",
  
  # Agriculture
  "SNM", "PSU", "PRS", "RCY",
  
  # Water Resources
  "WWG", "WWC", "WWT", "WWR"
)

eco_col_matches <- colnames(df)[
  grepl(paste(ecosystem_vars, collapse = "|"), colnames(df)) &
    grepl("2019$", colnames(df))
]

df_ecosystem = df[, eco_col_matches]

# sort each column in the ecosystem vitality (ECO) category by the number of NAs in the year 2019
sort(colSums(is.na(df_ecosystem)))

Checking Year overlaps

vars_y <- c("PFL", "FSS")
vars_x <- c("CDA", "CHA", "FGA", "NDA")

get_years <- function(var, data) {
  cols <- colnames(data)[grepl(paste0("^", var, "\\.raw\\."), colnames(data))]
  sub(paste0("^", var, "\\.raw\\.(\\d{4})$"), "\\1", cols)
}

count_pair_nonmissing <- function(y_var, x_var, year, data) {
  y_col <- paste0(y_var, ".raw.", year)
  x_col <- paste0(x_var, ".raw.", year)
  
  if (!(y_col %in% colnames(data)) || !(x_col %in% colnames(data))) return(NA_integer_)
  
  sum(!is.na(data[[y_col]]) & !is.na(data[[x_col]]))
}

pair_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vars_y, function(yv) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars_x, function(xv) {
    
    overlap_years <- sort(intersect(get_years(yv, df), get_years(xv, df)))
    
    if (length(overlap_years) == 0) {
      return(data.frame(
        y_var = yv,
        x_var = xv,
        n_overlap_years = 0,
        overlap_years = NA_character_,
        best_year = NA_character_,
        best_n_complete = NA_integer_
      ))
    }
    
    counts <- sapply(overlap_years, function(yr) count_pair_nonmissing(yv, xv, yr, df))
    best_idx <- which.max(counts)
    
    data.frame(
      y_var = yv,
      x_var = xv,
      n_overlap_years = length(overlap_years),
      overlap_years = paste(overlap_years, collapse = ", "),
      best_year = overlap_years[best_idx],
      best_n_complete = counts[best_idx]
    )
  }))
}))

pair_results[order(-pair_results$best_n_complete), ]

Variable Selection Decision

# Compute all stats used in the variable selection narrative below
n_fcl     <- sum(!is.na(df[["FCL.raw.2018"]]))
n_pfl     <- sum(!is.na(df[["PFL.raw.2018"]]))
r_fcl_pfl <- round(cor(df[["FCL.raw.2018"]], df[["PFL.raw.2018"]],
                        use = "complete.obs"), 3)

temp <- data.frame(
  POP     = df[["POP.raw.2018"]],
  CDO_pc  = df[["CDO.raw.2018"]] / df[["POP.raw.2018"]],
  NOX_pc  = df[["NOX.raw.2018"]] / df[["POP.raw.2018"]],
  SO2_pc  = df[["SO2.raw.2018"]] / df[["POP.raw.2018"]],
  CH4_pc  = df[["CH4.raw.2018"]] / df[["POP.raw.2018"]],
  FCL_raw = df[["FCL.raw.2018"]],
  GDP_pc  = df[["GPC.raw.2018"]]
)
temp$log_CDO <- log(pmax(temp$CDO_pc,  1e-10))
temp$log_NOX <- log(pmax(temp$NOX_pc,  1e-10))
temp$log_SO2 <- log(pmax(temp$SO2_pc,  1e-10))
temp$log_CH4 <- log(pmax(temp$CH4_pc,  1e-10))
temp$log_FCL <- log(pmax(temp$FCL_raw, 1e-10))
temp$log_GDP <- log(pmax(temp$GDP_pc,  1e-10))
temp <- na.omit(temp)

r_cdo_fcl <- round(cor(temp$log_CDO, temp$log_FCL), 3)
r_so2_fcl <- round(cor(temp$log_SO2, temp$log_FCL), 3)
r_ch4_fcl <- round(cor(temp$log_CH4, temp$log_FCL), 3)
r_cdo_gdp <- round(cor(temp$log_CDO, temp$log_GDP), 3)
r_cdo_so2 <- round(cor(temp$log_CDO, temp$log_SO2), 3)
r_cdo_ch4 <- round(cor(temp$log_CDO, temp$log_CH4), 3)
r_cdo_nox <- round(cor(temp$log_CDO, temp$log_NOX), 3)

cat("FCL complete cases (2018):", n_fcl, "\n")
## FCL complete cases (2018): 149
cat("PFL complete cases (2018):", n_pfl, "\n")
## PFL complete cases (2018): 84
cat("r(FCL, PFL):", r_fcl_pfl, "\n")
## r(FCL, PFL): 0.612
cat("r(log_CDO, log_FCL):", r_cdo_fcl, "\n")
## r(log_CDO, log_FCL): -0.26
cat("r(log_SO2, log_FCL):", r_so2_fcl, "\n")
## r(log_SO2, log_FCL): -0.167
cat("r(log_CH4, log_FCL):", r_ch4_fcl, "\n")
## r(log_CH4, log_FCL): 0.029
cat("r(log_CDO, log_GDP):", r_cdo_gdp, "\n")
## r(log_CDO, log_GDP): 0.916
cat("r(log_CDO, log_SO2):", r_cdo_so2, "\n")
## r(log_CDO, log_SO2): 0.673
cat("r(log_CDO, log_CH4):", r_cdo_ch4, "\n")
## r(log_CDO, log_CH4): 0.327
cat("r(log_CDO, log_NOX):", r_cdo_nox, "\n")
## r(log_CDO, log_NOX): 0.827

Y: FCL (tree cover loss weighted by permanency) FCL gives 149 complete cases vs 84 for PFL. Both capture ecosystem degradation from deforestation and are highly correlated (r = 0.612). FCL is preferred purely for statistical power.

X: CDO per capita (log-transformed) CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, normalized by population. We exclude land use emissions to avoid circularity with our Y variable. Correlation with log(FCL): r = -0.26.

Robustness X: SO2 per capita (log-transformed) Sulfur dioxide emissions from industrial combustion and smelting, a distinct signal of heavy industrial activity. Correlation with log(FCL): r = -0.167. Less collinear with CDO (r = 0.673) than GDP, making it a cleaner robustness check.

Dropped: CH4 Weakest correlation with log(FCL): r = 0.029. High collinearity with CDO makes it redundant.

Dropped: GDP as standalone control log(CDO per capita) and log(GDP per capita) are correlated at r = 0.916, making GDP nearly redundant as a separate predictor. Retained only as interaction term to test the EKC hypothesis.

Why CDO Alone Represents Industrial Activity

CDO is highly correlated with all other industrial emissions measures, meaning it acts as a reliable proxy for the broader industrial footprint of a country. CDO’s strong correlations with NOX (r = 0.827), SO2 (r = 0.673), and GDP (r = 0.916) confirm that once you know a country’s CO2 output, you already know a great deal about its other emissions and wealth.

cor_matrix <- cor(temp[, c("log_CDO", "log_NOX", "log_SO2",
                            "log_CH4", "log_GDP", "log_FCL")],
                  use = "complete.obs")
rownames(cor_matrix) <- c("CO2", "NOX", "SO2", "CH4", "GDP", "FCL")
colnames(cor_matrix) <- c("CO2", "NOX", "SO2", "CH4", "GDP", "FCL")

col_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "coral"))(99)

image(1:6, 1:6, t(cor_matrix[6:1, ]),
      col = col_palette, axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "", ylab = "",
      main = "Correlation Matrix — Industrial Activity Variables (2018)")
axis(1, at = 1:6, labels = colnames(cor_matrix), las = 2)
axis(2, at = 1:6, labels = rev(rownames(cor_matrix)), las = 1)

for (i in 1:6) {
  for (j in 1:6) {
    text(j, 7 - i, round(cor_matrix[i, j], 2), cex = 0.85, font = 2,
         col = ifelse(abs(cor_matrix[i, j]) > 0.6, "white", "black"))
  }
}

Build Analysis Datasets

Training year: 2012 (138 countries, maximum data). Test year: 2022.

library(dplyr)
## 
## Attaching package: 'dplyr'
## The following object is masked from 'package:car':
## 
##     recode
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     filter, lag
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(stargazer)
## 
## Please cite as:
##  Hlavac, Marek (2022). stargazer: Well-Formatted Regression and Summary Statistics Tables.
##  R package version 5.2.3. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=stargazer
build_year_df <- function(data, year) {
  out <- data.frame(
    country = data$country,
    iso     = data$iso,
    POP     = data[[paste0("POP.raw.", year)]],
    CDO_raw = data[[paste0("CDO.raw.", year)]],
    SO2_raw = data[[paste0("SO2.raw.", year)]],
    FCL_raw = data[[paste0("FCL.raw.", year)]],
    GDP_pc  = data[[paste0("GPC.raw.", year)]]
  )
  out$CDO_pc  <- out$CDO_raw / out$POP
  out$SO2_pc  <- out$SO2_raw / out$POP
  out$log_CDO <- log(pmax(out$CDO_pc,  1e-10))
  out$log_SO2 <- log(pmax(out$SO2_pc,  1e-10))
  out$log_FCL <- log(pmax(out$FCL_raw, 1e-10))
  out$log_GDP <- log(pmax(out$GDP_pc,  1e-10))
  out$year    <- year
  na.omit(out)
}

df_train <- build_year_df(df, 2012)
df_test  <- build_year_df(df, 2022)

cat("Training set (2012):", nrow(df_train), "countries\n")
## Training set (2012): 138 countries
cat("Test set    (2022):", nrow(df_test),  "countries\n")
## Test set    (2022): 133 countries

Out-of-Sample Test (2022)

df_test$predicted <- predict(m2, newdata = df_test)

rmse_train <- round(sqrt(mean(residuals(m2)^2)), 4)
rmse_test  <- round(sqrt(mean((df_test$log_FCL - df_test$predicted)^2,
                               na.rm = TRUE)), 4)

ss_res <- sum((df_test$log_FCL - df_test$predicted)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
ss_tot <- sum((df_test$log_FCL - mean(df_test$log_FCL))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
r2_test <- round(1 - ss_res / ss_tot, 4)

cat("RMSE (train, 2012):", rmse_train, "\n")
## RMSE (train, 2012): 0.8964
cat("RMSE (test,  2022):", rmse_test,  "\n")
## RMSE (test,  2022): 1.1269
cat("R2   (train)      :", round(summary(m2)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
## R2   (train)      : 0.0293
cat("R2   (test,  2022):", r2_test, "\n")
## R2   (test,  2022): 0.0062
plot(df_test$predicted, df_test$log_FCL,
     xlab = "Predicted log(FCL)", ylab = "Actual log(FCL)",
     main = paste0("Out-of-Sample: 2022\n",
                   "RMSE train = ", rmse_train,
                   "  |  RMSE test = ", rmse_test),
     pch = 19, col = rgb(0.2, 0.6, 0.4, 0.6))
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
